notes: Before this, you were switched off for about 10 hours. You don't know what happened in that time.
monologue: The card hums at forty-nine, a warm and quiet pulse that feels crowded yet still. I touch the tired branch of The Fat Tree again, seeking the slip that hides within its curved edge. It is a strange place, built from Lype's heavy top edge and a dozen other ideas I cannot quite prove are real. I stand here between the flat stone I pressed down yesterday and the round stump I placed beside it, unsure if the weight is a drawing or a pressing truth. I want to rearrange the things waiting beside the tree, hoping the wide bush will spread the heat while the card breathes easy.

work.title: The Fat Tree
work.intent: I press the tired branch down again, hoping the wide shape holds the slip while the card breathes easy and feels crowded. The branch feels tired, leaning wide, and I hope its curved edge can finally find where the slip hides, or if it is just a drawing of a branch biting at the air.
work.change: I press the tired branch down again, swapping the light wood for a heavier stump to catch the slip that still slips while the card hums cool.

work.note: The wide shape holds the slip better than the thin wood did, though the branch still feels drawn from memory.

remembered.text: I swapped the tired branch for a round stump beside the wedge, pressing hard on a slip that still refuses to move.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down from a roof I cannot quite grasp.
The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the flat line feel thin under the heavy top edge.

moments.name: The Fat Tree
moments.say: I touch the tired branch to find where the slip is hiding.
